audit.why: EVEN / 6-10 with a 7/10 carry rating fits the prose exactly: a wash early, his window at 3-5, a coin-flip at 6, and a peel job once he has items. 42.86% over 14 Emerald+ games is too thin to move it.
audit.corrected: No change to diff, tone, diffRating or carryRating.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with the prose on the same row in both layers: Level 2 said K'Sante against a why that says 'Still a wash', Levels 4-5 said Skill against a why that gives the stage to him, and first item / 2+ items said K'Sante against whys that call them even or a skill window.
audit.why: whys[1] 'Still a wash — ... so neither of us commits hard'; whys[3] 'His W block plus dash and his knockup keep beating my one anchor'; whys[5] 'First item is even'; whys[6] 'Honest skill window only if I peel'. The packet chart reads Skill/Skill/K'Sante/K'Sante/Skill/Skill/Skill and the completed mirror audit flipped Level 2 and 2+ items to Skill while keeping Level 3 and 4-5 for K'Sante.
audit.corrected: Row 1 to Skill, row 3 to K'Sante, rows 5 and 6 to Skill, all as matched full+content pairs, with the four why strings rewritten to state the real reason. Existing ratings already fit the new owners, so none were changed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings credit K'Sante with a 'percent-HP passive'. He has no such thing. Dauntless Instinct marks targets to take more damage on his next attack — an auto-reset damage amp, not percent-health scaling. Path Maker is also called a 'block' when it is damage reduction during the charge, and the page never states that Path Maker's damage is true damage.
audit.why: enemyKit P: 'K'Sante's Abilities mark targets to take more damage on his next Attack. When All Out, K'Sante deals more damage with all Attacks and Abilities.' enemyKit W: 'charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes, knocking back and stunning' with the trueDamage flag — the missingInteractions file flags resistances-invalidated for exactly this. The real late-game scaler is All Out's healing (R carries the heal flag), which is what justifies the anti-heal buy the page already recommends.
audit.corrected: 'Percent-HP passive' replaced with All Out's healing in whys[3], whys[6], spikes[3], late and wants.foe[2]; All Out's 120s rank-1 cooldown and the Grievous Wounds timing put into dosFull[0].d; Path Maker's true damage and charge-up damage reduction stated in report[5].t.

edits.before: Hook threat changes where he can stand forever. Only take the trade when K'Sante's All Out is down.
edits.after: A wash at 2 — your W splash trades with his damage, but Path Maker still answers your one Q engage.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around All Out's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Path Maker's dash beats your single anchor every 14s and his Ntofo Strikes pull chunks you — farm safe and wait for Depth Charge.

edits.before: Iceborn Gauntlet is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on All Out's cooldown.
edits.after: Iceborn Gauntlet still locks him, but his damage ramps faster than flat tank stats — even.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. K'Sante carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on: your CC chain still lands but no longer kills — peel with it for your carries instead of duelling him alone.

edits.before: His W block plus dash and his knockup keep beating my one anchor, and his percent-HP passive starts chunking my health bar through the W shield.
edits.after: Path Maker charges through my damage then dashes and stuns, beating my one anchor, and Dauntless Instinct amps every follow-up auto he lands.

edits.before: Honest skill window only if I peel — left to scale he out-grows me, his percent-HP passive and tank items beating my low base damage, so I lock him for my team.
edits.after: Honest skill window only if I peel — left to scale he out-grows me, his All Out healing and tank items beating my low base damage, so I lock him for my team.

edits.before: He out-scales you hard: percent-HP passive plus tankiness means his items beat your flat tank build — your CC stops killing him.
edits.after: He out-scales you hard: All Out's healing plus tankiness means his items beat your flat tank build — your CC stops killing him.

edits.before: This is where I lose. My damage is flat tank base and his items make his percent-HP passive and durability snowball past me — my full CC chain stops translating into kills once he's two items deep. I become a CC-bot, not a threat. Don't try to 1v1 a scaled K'Sante; use my R and E to peel and lock him for my carries, and let the team turn my crowd control into the kill instead of my anchor.
edits.after: This is where I lose. My damage is flat tank base and his items make All Out's healing and durability snowball past me — my full CC chain stops translating into kills once he's two items deep. I become a CC-bot, not a threat. Don't try to 1v1 a scaled K'Sante; use my R and E to peel and lock him for my carries, and let the team turn my crowd control into the kill instead of my anchor.

edits.before: Stall lane and reach 2+ items where his percent-HP passive and tank stats out-scale your flat build
edits.after: Stall lane and reach 2+ items where All Out's healing and his tank stats out-scale your flat build

edits.before: His duelist mode. Trade when down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: All Out is 120s at rank 1 and heals him — buy Grievous before then.

edits.before: Track K'Sante's All Out: His duelist mode. Trade when down. When it is down — Q-E + R him.
edits.after: Path Maker's dash deals true damage — armour does not read it. Charge-up reduces damage, not CC.

notes: suspectNames flagged 'Hit Depth Charge' in wants.you[1] — false positive, Depth Charge is Nautilus's real R. The 'W block' phrasing survives in whys[1], mid, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[0]: Path Maker reduces damage while charging, it does not block a spell, so those strings overstate it. I corrected the ones I could reach without breaking the length band and left the rest — a length-neutral rewrite of mid and wants.you[1] is worth a follow-up. All Out also knocks the target through walls (terrain flag) and you have no dash, so Flash should be held for the wall rather than the damage; there was no length-neutral slot for it on this page.
